question: Is my house eligible for solar panels?

confidence.text: Low: Haringey has not published its conservation area Article 4 directions, so one could exist.

limitations: This council has not published Article 4 directions for conservation areas, so a missing record proves nothing. Ask the council.
The share of solar power used at home follows the MCS tables for 2,500 kWh a year (a typical home, Ofgem); your own pattern may differ.
Rules for England, demo data for London.
Roof size and yield come from 1 m LIDAR and PVGIS: an installer's survey confirms them.
solar.next_step: Ask Haringey's planning team whether an Article 4 direction removes the right to add solar panels here.

facts.value: SE, 4.1 kWp, about 3927 kWh a year
facts.source: PVGIS 5.2, EU Joint Research Centre via Zetaris; roof from EA LIDAR

rules.clause: GPDO Sch 2 Part 14 Class A, A.2(c)
rules.plain: On a pitched roof, panels may stand up to 20 cm proud of the roof and may not go above the ridge.

rules.clause: GPDO Sch 2 Part 14 Class A, A.2(e)
rules.plain: In a conservation area, panels may not go on a wall, balcony or roof enclosure that faces a road. The roof is fine.

lines.one: Haringey has not published Article 4 directions for Muswell Hill Conservation Area, so we cannot rule one out.
lines.why: This house is not listed and sits in Muswell Hill Conservation Area. Panels on the south east roof slope (36°) would be permitted development unless an Article 4 direction removes that right, and Haringey keeps that record itself.
lines.get: Your south east roof slope (36°) could make about 3,927 kWh a year from about 4.1 kWp if Haringey says yes.
lines.cost: If Haringey says yes: about £6,500 to £8,600 to install 4.1 kWp, worth about £340 to £690 a year.

house_facts.label: Sun on the roof
house_facts.value: about 3,927 kWh a year from 4.1 kWp

challenges: No Article 4 that touches energy upgrades is on record for this house. Councils publish unevenly, so that alone is not proof. Does Haringey publish conservation area Article 4s at all?
One cost figure would hide how much prices vary. Check the national median against the London average before quoting a cost.
One share of solar power used at home would hide that it depends on who is home in the day. Ask the MCS tables for all three occupancy types, for this roof and a typical yearly use.
